record.title: ACCT reports cross-model context-state transfer across three model families
record.summary: A preprint introduces ACCT, which converts KV states already computed by one model into sparse KV states that a different-size model in the same family can use without re-encoding the full context. Across six directed pairs in Qwen3, Llama and Qwen2.5, authors report 4x KV-slot compression and mixed task results. The 6.5–21.2x speed headline measures conversion against target prefill and excludes source-model prefill. Appendix K includes source prefill: at the longest tested context, only three smaller-to-larger directions are faster than target-only prefill, while reverse directions are slower. These are author-reported experiments, not independent production evidence.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors posted arXiv:2610.42116v1 on 2026-10-30 describing ACCT, a method for converting source-model KV states into sparse target-model states within the same model family.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors evaluate six directed model pairs across Qwen3, Llama and Qwen2.5 and report context transfer with a 4x KV-slot budget. At about 19K tokens, transfer conversion alone is 6.5–21.2x faster than target context prefill; task performance varies by direction and benchmark, and often falls below the target-full baseline.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The conversion-only speed comparison excludes the time needed to prefill the context with the source model. Appendix K reports that when source-state prefill is included at the longest context, only three smaller-to-larger directions are faster than target-only prefill; reverse directions are slower. The paper does not establish production-scale throughput, quality parity generally or independent replication.

evidence_gaps.description: No accessible implementation or independent reproduction was established during targeted review.
Production concurrency, longer contexts, model-family transfer and task-quality preservation beyond the reported settings are unestablished.

brief.importance_rationale: If validated in workloads that repeatedly reuse context across model sizes, cross-scale KV transfer could reduce duplicated prefill and affect heterogeneous inference design. The paper’s value is presently a bounded feasibility result with mixed quality and direction-dependent total latency.
limitations: All reported outcomes are from the authors; no independent reproduction was performed.
The 6.5–21.2x headline excludes source-context prefill; complete costs depend on whether those source states already exist.
With source prefill included, only three smaller-to-larger directions beat target-only prefill at the longest tested context; reverse directions are slower.
Task results are mixed, with several settings materially below the target-full baseline; evaluation is limited to six directed within-family pairs and contexts around 19K tokens.
brief.summary: A preprint introduces ACCT, which converts KV states already computed by one model into sparse KV states that a different-size model in the same family can use without re-encoding the full context. Across six directed pairs in Qwen3, Llama and Qwen2.5, authors report 4x KV-slot compression and mixed task results. The 6.5–21.2x speed headline measures conversion against target prefill and excludes source-model prefill. Appendix K includes source prefill: at the longest tested context, only three smaller-to-larger directions are faster than target-only prefill, while reverse directions are slower. These are author-reported experiments, not independent production evidence.

technical.claimed_result: The paper reports conversion-only speedups of 6.5–21.2x versus target context prefill and mixed performance over 11 benchmarks/six context tasks. With source prefill included at the longest context, only three smaller-to-larger directions beat target-only prefill; reverse directions are slower.
technical.compute_or_cost: Reported speed compares state conversion against target prefill. Appendix K separately accounts for source prefill when source states are unavailable; the advantage depends on model direction and whether source states are already cached.
technical.demonstrated_result: The authors published a preprint detailing the method and evaluation. Reported performance and timing outcomes are not independently reproduced.
technical.mechanism: A three-part interface scores context tokens for target layers and heads, allocates a shared KV budget, and converts selected source representations to target-readable sparse KV. The target can then answer using transferred states without processing the original context again.
technical.regime: Authors test six directed pairs within Qwen3, Llama and Qwen2.5, at contexts up to approximately 19K tokens and 4x KV-slot compression. Timing uses batch size one on 8×A800 80GB hardware with medians over two or three runs. A separately trained interface is used for each direction.
technical.strongest_baseline: Target Full is the task-performance reference and target-only context prefill is the timing reference. Comparisons are author-run and do not establish production throughput or costs.

brief.title: ACCT reports cross-model context-state transfer across three model families
brief.why_it_matters: If cross-scale context reuse can preserve task quality while lowering total compute in repeated-context workloads, it could change how heterogeneous model systems route long conversations and documents. The paper provides a bounded feasibility result across three model families, but conversion-only latency overstates the advantage when source context states must first be constructed, and reported task performance is mixed.
